text:
Alex: CI is red on the canary pipeline — image publish failing during push to registry-proxy (us-west). Getting a 502 and then a manifest validation error. Can someone triage?

Priya: I hit this too. It started right after I merged the Dockerfile reorder (moved some COPYs up). Build succeeds locally but push fails in CI. Error snippet from CI: `rpc error: code = Unknown desc = unexpected status: 502 Bad Gateway` then `manifest put failed: unexpected EOF`

Sam: 502 from the proxy usually indicates a transient upstream (s3 or registry backend) or an intermediary (bastion) choking on the chunked upload. Did the push include very large layers?

Jen: Not particularly large, typical app image ~420MB. I added retries to the push step and reran one job just now — it still failed at the same point. Logs: ```
# docker push log tail
Pushing layer sha256:... done
Pushing layer sha256:... 3/4
error: write tcp 10.10.0.5:443->10.20.0.2:54012: write: connection reset by peer
manifest put http error: unexpected EOF
```

Morgan: Are we on the new registry proxy autoscaling group? There was a token rotation yesterday but should be transparent. Worth checking proxy pods for 502 spikes. I can check infra metrics.

ci-bot: build #5823 failed: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/5823 - docker-publish step. Full logs attached.

Priya: I noticed the Dockerfile reorder changed layer boundaries: earlier we had `COPY --from=builder /app/dist /app/dist` after some apt installs; now it's before which reduces the layer dedupe. Could be exposing a registry cache bug where identical layer digests collide and a subsequent write fails. Weird but plausible.

Alex: Two asks: (1) quick triage to decide whether to rerun/downgrade canary, (2) bisect whether the Dockerfile change introduced the failure. Who can do a bisect?

Sam: I'll bisect. Plan: run CI push for commit range from HEAD~12..HEAD and see the first commit that starts failing. Will coordinate manual reruns to avoid consuming many builder slots. If it's flaky we'll try pushing the same image via buildkit on a jumpbox to see if registry behaves differently.

Jen: I can run a manual build+push from a dev bastion (buildkit) now to check proxy behavior. If that succeeds, points to CI network/path. If it fails the same, likely registry backend or layer mutation issue.

(Minutes later)

Jen: Manual build+push from bastion succeeded (same commit as CI). Push went through, digest published: sha256:abcd... Suggests CI path/proxy is the problem.

Morgan: Confirmed proxy pod `registry-proxy-6f7c9` restarted around the same time as failures and CPU spiked. There are a bunch of transient 502s in proxy logs with stack traces around chunked uploads. Filing infra ticket.

Priya: Given that, bisecting still useful to see why this surfaced now (Dockerfile change might change upload timing/parallelism). Sam, if your bisect shows earlier commits were fine on CI that is strong evidence of CI/proxy flip vs Dockerfile.

Sam: Starting bisect now. I will keep the range tight: HEAD~8..HEAD. Will annotate which commits reran and results. If a commit flips, we can try toggling the Dockerfile order locally to reproduce the timing effect.

Alex: Short-term mitigation: can we add a conservative retry/backoff on the publish step in CI (3 retries with 30s backoff) and gate canary on manual approval until infra fixes proxy? I don't want noisy CI failures to block merges.

Jen: +1 to retry in CI. I'll open the PR to add `--max-concurrent-uploads=1` to the push or add retries depending on the executor. For buildkit `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build` you can set `--max-concurrent-uploads` in the daemon or use `--max-parallelism` depending on tooling. I'll test.

Morgan: Infra ticket: INFRA-3218 created (registry-proxy chunked-upload 502s). Assigning to network and proxy teams. Attaching proxy logs and pod restart timeline.

Sam: Bisect update: first failing commit identified at HEAD~3 (the Dockerfile reorder commit by Priya). Re-running that older commit on CI failed too. But manual bastion push succeeded for that commit as well. So it's likely the Dockerfile change increases parallel upload concurrency which triggers the proxy bug.

Priya: Ok that explains it. I'll revert the reorder in a small PR and we can see if CI returns to green, or we can apply the CI push backoff as a quicker mitigation.

Alex: Action items: Jen to open CI retry/backoff PR (short-lived), Priya to open revert PR for Dockerfile reorder, Morgan/infra to debug and patch proxy (INFRA-3218), Sam to finish bisect notes and paste results in the ticket. We'll gate canary until CI is stable.

Priya: Thanks all. Sorry for the churn — I'll keep the revert tiny and reference this thread.

Alex: Thanks. Marking thread resolved when canary is back to green. :thumbsup:
